title: One codon changes
hook: Predict the result, then reveal the sequence.

knows: DNA and RNA are sequences of chemical building blocks.
doesNotKnow: Both GAA and GAG encode glutamate in the standard genetic code. This single-base change is synonymous for the amino-acid sequence, though it may have other effects.

misconception: The original sequence and the resulting sequence must have the same interpretation.
objective: Both GAA and GAG encode glutamate in the standard genetic code. This single-base change is synonymous for the amino-acid sequence, though it may have other effects.

claims.text: Question, answer, diagram and explanation: In the standard genetic code, a codon changes from GAA to GAG. What happens to its amino acid? Both GAA and GAG encode glutamate in the standard genetic code. This single-base change is synonymous for the amino-acid sequence, though it may have other effects.
Recall: In the standard genetic code, can two different codons encode the same amino acid? The genetic code is redundant: for example GAA and GAG both encode glutamate.
